title: SEBot: Structural Entropy Guided Multi-View Contrastive learning for Social Bot Detection

problem.claim: Social bot detection must distinguish benign and bot accounts that influence one another within a social interaction graph.

gap.claim: Transductive message-passing methods may underuse hidden graph information, be vulnerable to adversarial bot behavior, and produce overly homogeneous representations by indiscriminately passing messages across categories and communities.

contributions.claim: SEBot is a multi-view graph-based contrastive-learning social bot detector.
The method uses structural entropy to optimize graph and subgraph-level structure and reveal implicit hierarchical community structure.
The method combines an encoder designed for message passing beyond homophily with multi-view contrastive learning and multi-task learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SEBot as a novel multi-view graph-based contrastive-learning social bot detector.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments reportedly show that the approach significantly improves social bot detection performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Neural Networks have driven recent advances in social bot detection.
Social interaction graphs contain mutually influencing benign and bot accounts.
Existing transductive graph methods may miss hidden structure, resist adversarial behavior poorly, and homogenize node representations.
SEBot applies structural entropy, beyond-homophily message passing, and multi-view contrastive multi-task learning.
The authors report improved performance over state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: Indiscriminate message passing across categories and communities can make node representations excessively homogeneous.

interpretation.claim: Graph detectors may benefit from modeling structural uncertainty and community hierarchy instead of relying only on local homophily.

application.claim: For graph-based detection tasks, consider structure-aware views and message-passing mechanisms that remain effective beyond homophily.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when these design choices fail or generalize beyond social bot detection.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the structural entropy optimization procedure in detail.
Robustness to adversarial behavior is not independently verified.
